original_question: Consider a multigeometric series (k_1, ..., k_m; 1/n) with integer coefficients k_i, with none of k_1, ..., k_m divisible by n, and let Sigma = {sigma_0 < ... < sigma_{n-1}} be the set of all subsums of {k_1, ..., k_m}, assumed to have exactly n elements. If the achievement set E(k_1, ..., k_m; 1/n) has positive Lebesgue measure and sigma_i is congruent to t_i modulo n with t_i < n, must the set of residues {t_i} equal {0, 1, ..., n-1}?
target_in_paper: Conjecture 1.1, in the residue-class reformulation supplied by Proposition 1.2, concerning the critical-ratio case q=1/n for multigeometric achievement sets with exactly n distinct one-block subsums.
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the core mathematical content: the critical case q=1/n, the assumption that the one-block digit set Sigma coming from subsums of k_1,...,k_m has exactly n elements, the positive-Lebesgue-measure hypothesis for the achievement set E(k_1,...,k_m;1/n), and the intended conclusion that Sigma should represent all residue classes modulo n. It is also faithful to the paper's residue-language reformulation by ordering Sigma as {sigma_0<...<sigma_{n-1}} and writing sigma_i ≡ t_i (mod n).
missing_details: The coefficients should be stated as positive integers k_1,...,k_m, not merely arbitrary integers.
The integer parameter n should be quantified explicitly, with n >= 2.
Sigma should be defined explicitly as the set of all one-block subsums Sigma = {sum_{i=1}^m epsilon_i k_i : epsilon_i in {0,1}}.
The assumption |Sigma| = n should be stated as meaning that these subsums are distinct up to exactly n values.

The achievement set should be defined explicitly, not just named: E(k_1,...,k_m;1/n) is the set of all subsums of the multigeometric sequence (k_1,...,k_m;1/n), equivalently the self-similar set generated by the digit set Sigma at ratio 1/n.
The ambient measure space should be made explicit: positive Lebesgue measure means positive one-dimensional Lebesgue measure on R.
The residues t_i should be specified as the standard representatives in {0,1,...,n-1}.
To match the paper-faithful sharp formulation, the conclusion should be stated as 'Sigma is a complete residue system modulo n' or equivalently '{t_0,...,t_{n-1}} = {0,1,...,n-1}'.
The question should remain narrowly at the critical ratio q=1/n and should not be broadened to general q or to arbitrary self-similar digit sets beyond the nearby formulation in the paper.
refined_question:
Let n >= 2 and let k_1,...,k_m be positive integers such that none of k_1,...,k_m is divisible by n. Define
Sigma := {sum_{i=1}^m epsilon_i k_i : epsilon_i in {0,1}},
and assume that |Sigma| = n. Write Sigma = {sigma_0 < sigma_1 < ... < sigma_{n-1}}, and for each i let t_i in {0,1,...,n-1} be the residue determined by sigma_i ≡ t_i (mod n). If the achievement set of the multigeometric sequence (k_1,...,k_m;1/n), namely E(k_1,...,k_m;1/n), has positive Lebesgue measure in R, must Sigma be a complete residue system modulo n; equivalently, must {t_0,...,t_{n-1}} = {0,1,...,n-1}?
equivalent_formulation: Under the same assumptions, does lambda(E(k_1,...,k_m;1/n)) > 0 imply that the digit set Sigma = {sum_{i=1}^m epsilon_i k_i : epsilon_i in {0,1}} is congruent modulo n to {0,1,...,n-1}?
justification: This is the narrowest stand-alone version of your draft that stays aligned with the paper's introductory formulation: the main target is the conjectural positive-measure criterion at the critical ratio q=1/n, while Proposition 1.2 supplies the residue-class reformulation in terms of the ordered subsum set Sigma = {sigma_0<...<sigma_{n-1}} and residues t_i. The nearby Theorem 1.3 is supporting context/partial evidence, so the refined question should remain at the conjecture level and should not be broadened beyond the exact q=1/n multigeometric setting.
